inventory.title: USGS runoff-generated postfire debris-flow inventory (Graber et al. 2026)
filters: All records: 8,981 records, 80 fires, 1,140 debris flows
PeakI15 present: 7,945 records, 78 fires, 1,044 debris flows
HM23 (T) present: 7,639 records, 77 fires, 955 debris flows
dNBR/1000 (F) present: 7,639 records, 77 fires, 955 debris flows
KF (S) present: 7,639 records, 77 fires, 955 debris flows
UpstreamArea present: 7,639 records, 77 fires, 955 debris flows
StormStart, DaysSinceFire and observation location present: 7,639 records, 77 fires, 955 debris flows

features.T: Proportion of the upstream area burned at moderate/high severity and steeper than 23° (inventory HM23)
features.F: Mean dNBR / 1000 of the upstream area (inventory dNBR/1000)
features.S: Mean soil KF-factor of the upstream area, STATSGO (inventory KF)
features.R15: Peak 15-minute rainfall accumulation, mm (= PeakI15 mm/h × 0.25)
features.log_area_km2: log10 of the upstream contributing area, km² (inventory UpstreamArea)
features.days_since_fire: Days from fire ignition to storm start; stands in for vegetation recovery (inventory DaysSinceFire). One value per fire and storm, so constant across a design-storm map
features.soil_moisture_0_7cm: Antecedent soil moisture 0–7 cm, m³/m³: ERA5-Land (Open-Meteo archive), mean of the UTC day before the storm. Varies only between 0.1° cells within a storm
features.ctx_T: Spatial context: mean T of the 5 nearest other watersheds in the same fire and storm (features only); used only by the mlp_context variant
features.ctx_F: Spatial context: mean F of the 5 nearest other watersheds in the same fire and storm (features only); used only by the mlp_context variant
features.ctx_S: Spatial context: mean S of the 5 nearest other watersheds in the same fire and storm (features only); used only by the mlp_context variant
features.ctx_R15: Spatial context: mean R15 of the 5 nearest other watersheds in the same fire and storm (features only); used only by the mlp_context variant

notes: The inventory covers 80 fires from 2000–2024 in AZ, CA, CO, MT, NM, UT, WA, WY. It has no 2025 fires, so it holds no observed debris-flow outcomes for Eaton or Palisades, and nothing here scores the models there: on the Risk tab the models are compared with USGS's assessment, which measures agreement with USGS, not accuracy.

Seven models: six are fitted and scored leave-one-fire-out; m1_published is not fitted here (no cross-validation): its published coefficients are scored only on records outside the inventory they were fitted on. on_map marks the models behind the map's columns: m1_refit (M1 recalibrated, m1_p_*) and rf_extended (rf_p_*); the map's usgs_p_* is USGS's own published M1. The MLPs are scored here but not mapped, because nothing constrains them to rise with rainfall.
Grizzly Creek contributes 1,426 of the 7,639 usable records (19%). Pooled metrics weight every record equally, so large fires dominate them; the per-fire median weights every fire equally.

Pooled ROC AUC mostly ranks records of different storms against each other: only 2% of the (debris flow, non-flow) pairs it compares lie within one fire and storm (3% on m1_published's records), and 73% of R15's variance lies between fire-storm groups. Per-fire ROC AUC also ranks a fire's storms against each other (46% of its pairs lie within one storm). A design-storm map ranks watersheds within one fire under one storm, so each model's within_storm is ROC AUC within each fire and storm that has both outcomes (99 such groups, 2,407 records; for m1_published, 64 groups, 1,672 records). On m1_published's records the trained models' within-storm median / record-weighted mean are: m1_refit 0.800 / 0.763, rf_m1vars 0.800 / 0.751, mlp_m1vars 0.750 / 0.736, rf_extended 0.825 / 0.783, mlp_extended 0.813 / 0.798, mlp_context 0.793 / 0.805, against m1_published 0.809 / 0.797. Most groups are small (median 10 records and 3 debris flows), so the median lands on fractions with small denominators; the record-weighted mean is less coarse.

Days since fire and antecedent soil moisture are storm-level: 0.0% and 2.9% of their variance lies within a fire and storm (soil moisture has a single value in 664 of the 1,052 fire-storm groups), against 63% for log area and 58% for T. On a design-storm map both are one value for every watershed, so they set the level of the likelihood there, not the ranking, and their permutation importance is credit for ranking storms, not watersheds.

The Risk tab's scenario storm comes 37 days after ignition; the usable records have a median of 336 days since fire. Only 950 of them (9 fires, 12 fire-storms, 198 debris flows) are from storms within 37 days of a fire, and 857 of those are one storm: the Thomas Fire's of 2018-01-09. What the extended models do at 37 days rests mostly on that one storm, so the level of rf_p_* under the scenario is an extrapolation from little data.

1,320 usable records (33 fires, including all 489 Station Fire records) come from the Staley et al. (2016) inventory M1 was fitted on, so m1_published is scored only on the other 6,319 and has no Station Fire analogue. On those same records the out-of-fold ROC AUCs of the trained models are: m1_refit 0.858, rf_m1vars 0.871, mlp_m1vars 0.839, rf_extended 0.858, mlp_extended 0.855, mlp_context 0.865.

On those 6,319 records M1's published likelihoods average 0.363 against an observed debris-flow rate of 0.098; on the 1,320 Staley et al. (2016) records they average 0.377 against 0.253. Its pooled ROC AUC (0.881) mostly credits ranking storms against each other (3% of the pairs lie within one fire and storm); within a fire and storm, the ranking a map shows, its median ROC AUC is 0.809 (record-weighted 0.797). Its likelihoods run high, far more on the newer records, which is what its Brier score reflects.

Absolute likelihood levels depend on how each sub-inventory sampled non-events: the observed debris-flow rate is 0.253 in the Staley et al. (2016) records and 0.098 in the rest (by PreviousUSGSInventory: Graber (2023) 0.106 (2,978 records), Rengers and others (2023) 0.022 (1,417 records), Staley and others (2016) 0.253 (1,320 records), Graber (2024) 0.112 (1,019 records), New data, this version 0.133 (737 records), Thomas and others (2023b) 0.383 (154 records), Thomas and others (2023a) 0.143 (14 records)). M1 recalibrated (m1_refit fitted on all 7,639 usable records) averages 0.125 overall, 0.151 on the Staley et al. (2016) records (observed 0.253) and 0.120 on the rest (observed 0.098), so its level follows the mix of sub-inventories it was fitted on; M1's published coefficients were fitted on the Staley et al. (2016) inventory alone. Neither level is an observed rate for a 2025 fire.

Grizzly Creek is 1,426 of those 6,319 records (23%). Without it (4,893 records) m1_published scores ROC AUC 0.860 and Brier 0.228, and the trained models' out-of-fold ROC AUCs on the same records are: m1_refit 0.834, rf_m1vars 0.847, mlp_m1vars 0.805, rf_extended 0.837, mlp_extended 0.841, mlp_context 0.860.

M1 recalibrated: M1's form refitted on all usable records gives B = -3.25, Ct = 0.26, Cf = -0.02, Cs = 0.34 (published: B = -3.63, Ct = 0.41, Cf = 0.67, Cs = 0.70). The refitted F·R coefficient is near zero and of the opposite sign to M1's: on this inventory mean dNBR adds little once T and S are in the model (on the log-odds scale the terms average T·R 0.57, F·R 0.04, S·R 0.44 in absolute value). It is saved as m1_refit, with these coefficients, in work/debris_flow/models.joblib; the per-fire step maps it as m1_p_*.

Cross-validation is leave-one-fire-out over 77 folds: every record of the held-out fire is unseen when the models are fitted. It is not unseen in the design of the variables: T's definition (moderate/high severity and steeper than 23°) and M1's interaction form were chosen by USGS on the Staley et al. (2016) inventory, which holds every Station Fire record, so the Station fold is held out from fitting, not from variable design. Per-fire ROC AUC needs both outcomes, so 25 fires with only debris flows or only non-flows are left out of it. Records of the same watershed in different storms are not independent; holding out whole fires keeps them together.

PR AUC is average precision. Hyperparameters were fixed before evaluation, not tuned on held-out fires: random forests of 300 trees with at least 5 records per leaf, constrained to be non-decreasing in R15 (scikit-learn monotonic_cst: +1 on R15, 0 elsewhere); MLPs with hidden layers of 32 and 16 units, L2 penalty 0.001 and early stopping on a random 10% of the training records held aside, on standardized inputs. No class reweighting.

A likelihood that falls when rain rises is unacceptable on a design-storm map, so the random forests are monotone in R15, as M1 is by its form. Check on all usable records at the seven design storms (I15 16–40 mm/h, every other feature as recorded), counting records whose likelihood falls between consecutive storms: the saved rf_extended, 0 of 7,639; the same forest fitted without the constraint, 5,893 (largest fall 0.145); the saved mlp_extended, 323 (largest fall 0.022).

Antecedent soil moisture: Open-Meteo archive API, models=era5_land, hourly soil_moisture_0_to_7cm (ECMWF ERA5-Land reanalysis, 0.1° grid), mean of the 24 UTC hours of the day before the storm, at the observation location (256 requests, one per fire and run of storm dates no more than 14 days apart). It is ~9 km reanalysis, not a measurement. All 7,639 records have a value; none needed imputing.

Spatial context is an evaluated variant, not one of the extended features: mlp_context adds the mean T, F, S and R15 of the 5 nearest other watersheds (by outlet) in the same fire and storm, from their features only, never their responses. Against mlp_extended it changes pooled ROC AUC by +0.007, Brier by +0.003, the per-fire median by +0.021, within-storm ROC AUC by -0.058 (median) and -0.003 (record-weighted), and Station ROC AUC by +0.031. Within storms it ranks no better than mlp_extended on either measure. Its context features' permutation importance: ctx_T 0.005, ctx_F 0.000, ctx_S 0.007, ctx_R15 0.086.

mlp_context is not mapped. Under a design storm every watershed gets the same I15, so ctx_R15 equals R15 everywhere (in the inventory it does in 56% of records). In the inventory the neighbours are observation points: 310 records alone in their storm use their own values, 1,255 have fewer than 5 neighbours, and 835 share their fire, storm and location with another (367 locations), so their nearest neighbour is 0 m away. The mean distance to the context neighbours has median 845 m (IQR 410–1,374 m); USGS's segment networks are much denser (step 15 reports their spacing), where the neighbours are segments upstream and downstream on the same channel and ties between equidistant segments change which are averaged. These quartiles are saved with the models.

Vegetation recovery from satellite NDVI is not included; days since fire stands in for it. Soil bulk density is not used: we had no per-watershed source for it across these fires, and a value constant within a fire would act as a fire identifier under leave-one-fire-out. Storm accumulation, duration, 30- and 60-minute intensities and rainfall ratios are not used: a design storm specifies only I15, and many records lack them.

Permutation importance is the drop in pooled out-of-fold ROC AUC when one feature is replaced by its value at a random record (mean of 3 permutations, each record still predicted by its own fold's model), so like pooled ROC AUC it mostly credits ranking storms. Correlated features share credit, so a small drop does not mean a feature is unused. A near-duplicate works the other way: in mlp_context, ctx_R15 correlates 0.94 with R15, so permuting it alone creates R15/ctx_R15 pairs that never occur, and its drop overstates what it adds on its own. Permuting R15 and ctx_R15 together drops mlp_context's ROC AUC by 0.272.
